title: Nonemptiness from Fourier concentration
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For each subset $S$, let $\widehat f(S)$ be the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$, and define its Fourier weight to be $\widehat f(S)^2$. If the sum of the Fourier weights over subsets outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$, then $\mathcal F$ is nonempty.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
The Fourier weight outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$
